    How the Comparison Works

    Both households start with the same cash. The buyer spends it on the down payment and fees, and the renter invests it. Each month, whichever household has lower housing costs invests the difference. At the end, the buyer's net worth is the home's sale value, less selling costs and the remaining loan, plus any investments. The renter's is the value of their investments.

    Example: An AED 1,500,000 home or AED 7,500 a month in rent, with the starting assumptions above. After 10 years, the buyer has AED 1,093,904 and the renter has AED 837,540, leaving buying ahead by AED 256,364.

    The model leaves out tax and assumes steady growth rates. Real prices and rents move unevenly, and a forced sale in a weak market can change the result.

    What Changes the Answer Most

    • How long you stay: a longer stay spreads the fees over more years
    • Price-to-rent ratio: the higher the price compared with the rent, the more renting tends to win
    • Home price growth: small changes compound into large differences over many years
    • Investment return: the renter only benefits if they really do invest the money
    • Your mortgage rate: try the rate after any fixed period ends, not just the introductory one

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Is it better to rent or buy in Dubai?
    It depends mainly on how long you will stay, the price compared with rent, and what your money could earn elsewhere. The upfront fees are large, so buying usually needs several years to pay off. The calculator shows when that happens on your assumptions.
    How long do I need to stay for buying to make sense?
    There is no fixed number. The fees of around 7% on a typical financed purchase, plus selling costs, need time to recover. A short expected stay favours renting, and your employment and visa position may matter as much as the maths.
    What ownership costs should I include?
    Include service charges, maintenance and insurance. Service charges vary widely between buildings, so check the Dubai Land Department's service charge index or the actual building's figures, then convert them into a yearly percentage of the price.
    What rate of home price growth should I use?
    Choose a cautious long-run figure and try a few. Past price rises in Dubai have come with sharp falls too, so a recent strong year is a poor guide. Compare a low, a medium and a high case.
    Why does the calculator invest the money for the renter?
    Because that is the true alternative. A renter keeps the deposit and fees, which could earn a return. Comparing rent with mortgage payments alone ignores that, and also ignores the debt the buyer repays and the value of the home.
